key_insight: Knowledge-graph grounding only helps LLMs when the needed fact is outside the model’s training; it adds little or nothing for already-known public biomedical facts.
clinical_relevance: For clinical QA systems, structured retrieval may be most useful for private, local, or newly emerging knowledge rather than for common public medical knowledge.
method: Reproduced a reported HealthBench result and checked the effect of a grader bug.
Tested graph+vector retrieval over PrimeKG with both triple retrieval and natural-language-to-Cypher querying.
Compared performance on MedQA, synthetic counterfactual KG facts, and a hybrid known-vs-novel benchmark across model sizes.
evidence_signal: Across the public KG setting, all gains were tiny (|Δ| ≤ 3.4), while the same pipeline boosted out-of-training accuracy from chance to nearly 100% on synthetic/hybrid novel facts.
watch_item: Results come from one public biomedical KG and one graph-retrieval pipeline, so performance may differ with other knowledge bases, query styles, or clinical use cases.
paper_title: Knowledge-Graph Grounding Helps LLMs Only for Out-of-Training Knowledge: A Controlled Study on Clinical Question Answering
